title: Personal Atari ST tools and C64 development discovery pass
summary: Personally screen 109 search hits, inspect fourteen new roots, add thirteen projects and defer one migrated source.
notes: Root performed this entire discovery and publication pass personally, without delegating research to a worker. Four fresh repository searches were screened against updated main before inspecting fourteen selected roots. BBC disassembly hits were already covered and not re-researched. Primary immutable files and actual implementation/build paths were reviewed; no upstream program was executed. Preserve root-level utility collections rather than fragment them, distinguish native ports from source-intake plans, note duplicate mirrored common libraries, and defer an inaccessible canonical-host migration. Build and hardware claims remain qualified; AI attribution is positive only where explicitly disclosed.

sources.reason: Repository-level port coordination, pinned upstream recipes and actual AGA/HAM8 support code for m68k AROS/AmigaOS. Do not split every planned port into a claimed delivered game. Root status distinguishes compiled, first-light, testing and release gates.
Native blitter sprite clipping/skew/masking routines with a C demo and PHP generators for palette, sprites and world data. Concrete implementation, not a title-specific completed Power Drift port.

Host-side SNDH diagnostics parses metadata and subtunes, checks termination/bounds and converts Atari text to Unicode; source includes ICE support. Current CLI reads and prints files, not an automatic music repair or playback claim.
Converts indexed 320x200 PNG pictures to Atari ST planar PI1, writes sixteen palette words and zeroed colour-cycle data, and checks a 32066-byte output length.
Converts Atari ST CyberPaint SEQ animations into animated GIF, with COPY/XOR frame composition and compressed/uncompressed word streams. Inspected frame conversion implementation.

MSA track decompression/compression and FAT12 inspection, listing, extraction and insertion with CLI and wxWidgets GUI sources; companion module scanning script. Actual codec and filesystem logic inspected.
Collection of Python/Tk and browser helpers for TOS relocation inspection, graphics/sample conversion and generated tables. Keep scope at root rather than separate records for each small script.

Native display-lag measurement aid synchronizes a screen counter with floppy/user LED transitions for high-frame-rate camera comparison. GFA BASIC listing contains the timing and palette/PSG accesses.
Original BASIC demake of Baba Is You with rule-word parsing, movement, undo and a small level editor. Five tutorial-level maps and concrete game logic are present.
Studio Ghibli-inspired acorn-catching game with one/two-player modes, sprite multiplexing and IRQ-driven music. Native implementation and assets are included.
Assembly side-scroller made for Arok party 2026 with scrolling, sword combat, effects and game assets. Inspected raster interrupt setup and gameplay source.

Halloween-themed C64 game with obstacle entities, sprites, collision logic and joystick/paddle input. Main TRSE source and included obstacle module are substantial, not only images or a binary release.
SID-oriented JSON patch editor, preview/export pipeline and native C64 audition support. Assembly exporter emits seven-byte effect records and separate sweep/vibrato tables for game integration.

Defer canonical-host migration check: GitHub README explicitly says the project moved to Codeberg, where graphics.dat support was added. The GitHub Python dungeon parser and example are concrete, but the destination was inaccessible in this review; retain the canonical source lead rather than silently track an obsolete mirror as current.
